question_text: Construct top_three(products) in Python. Each product has a price attribute and the list contains at least three products. Return three highest-priced product objects in descending price order, using selection sort. Do not modify the supplied list.
adaptation_rationale: Retains selection sort/objects/top-k reasoning; explicit minimum length avoids source under specification, Python copy protects input.

marking_points.criterion: Creates a separate working copy and returns its first three objects.
Performs three selection passes over positions 0..2.
Searches remaining positions for the maximum price.
Swaps selected object into the current output position, producing descending order.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent technically correct wording or valid implementation earning the specified independent points.
partial_credit_notes: Award each stated point independently up to the total; do not double-credit the same idea.

verification.technical: Concrete marking points independently reasoned from the defined context and exact 2027 scope.
verification.code_check: Executable checks saved under checks/ where applicable.

test_code:
from types import SimpleNamespace
items=[SimpleNamespace(price=x) for x in [4,9,1,7,5]];before=items[:]
assert [x.price for x in top_three(items)]==[9,7,5] and items==before
assert [x.price for x in top_three([SimpleNamespace(price=x) for x in [3,3,1]])]==[3,3,1]
